events.title: Wham-O is granted a patent for the Frisbee
events.summary: A US patent covers 'a saucer-shaped throwing implement'.
events.description: On December 26, 1967, the Wham-O Manufacturing Company was issued a US patent for what it called a saucer-shaped throwing implement, better known as the Frisbee.
events.notificationBody: In 1967, Wham-O was granted a patent for its flying disc, the Frisbee.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 26

events.title: Mao Zedong is born
events.summary: The future first chairman of the People's Republic of China is born.
events.description: On December 26, 1893, Mao Zedong was born. A Marxist theorist and revolutionary, he became the first chairman of the People's Republic of China, serving from 1949 to 1959.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 26

events.title: An earthquake off Sumatra triggers the Indian Ocean tsunami
events.summary: A massive undersea earthquake sends a devastating tsunami across the Indian Ocean.
events.description: On December 26, 2004, a massive earthquake shook the Indian Ocean floor west of the island of Sumatra, triggering a devastating tsunami that struck coastlines across the region.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 26

events.title: Charles Babbage is born in London
events.summary: The mathematician and inventor of early calculating machines is born.
events.description: On December 26, 1791, the mathematician and inventor Charles Babbage, a pioneer of mechanical computing, was born in London.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 26

events.title: Jack Johnson wins the world heavyweight title
events.summary: He becomes the first Black world heavyweight boxing champion.
events.description: On December 26, 1908, Jack Johnson defeated Tommy Burns in Sydney, Australia, to become the first Black fighter to win the world heavyweight boxing championship.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 26

events.title: Hagia Sophia is consecrated in Constantinople
events.summary: The great domed church becomes the largest in the world.
events.description: On December 27, 537, the Hagia Sophia in Constantinople was consecrated as a church. It was then the largest church in the world.
events.notificationTitle: A dome that awed an empire
events.notificationBody: In 537, the Hagia Sophia was consecrated in Constantinople.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 27

events.title: Charles Darwin sets sail on HMS Beagle
events.summary: The voyage will shape his theory of evolution.
events.description: On December 27, 1831, Charles Darwin set sail on HMS Beagle, beginning the voyage during which he would formulate his theory of evolution.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 27

events.title: Johannes Kepler is born
events.summary: The astronomer will discover three laws of planetary motion.
events.description: On December 27, 1571, the German astronomer Johannes Kepler was born. He discovered three major laws of planetary motion.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 27

events.title: The Netherlands transfers sovereignty to Indonesia
events.summary: Dutch control ends four years after Indonesia declared independence.
events.description: On December 27, 1949, the Dutch formally relinquished control over Indonesia, which had declared its independence in 1945.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 27

events.title: Benazir Bhutto is assassinated
events.summary: Pakistan's former prime minister is killed while campaigning.
events.description: On December 27, 2007, Benazir Bhutto, former prime minister of Pakistan, was assassinated in Rawalpindi while campaigning in parliamentary elections.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 27

events.title: The Lumiere brothers' Cinematographe makes its public debut
events.summary: Moving pictures are shown to the public at the Grand Cafe in Paris.
events.description: On December 28, 1895, the first public demonstration of the Lumiere brothers' Cinematographe took place at the Grand Cafe in Paris, a landmark in the birth of cinema.
events.notificationTitle: The first night at the movies
events.notificationBody: In 1895, the Lumiere brothers screened films to the public in Paris.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 28

events.title: Westminster Abbey is consecrated
events.summary: Edward the Confessor's church opens in London.
events.description: On December 28, 1065, Westminster Abbey in London was consecrated and opened by Edward the Confessor.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 28

events.title: The Indian National Congress meets for the first time
events.summary: The party that will lead India's independence movement holds its first session.
events.description: On December 28, 1885, the first session of the Indian National Congress convened. The party later led the movement for India's independence.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 28

events.title: Constance Markievicz becomes the first woman elected to the House of Commons
events.dateNote: The general election was held on December 14; results were declared on December 28.
events.summary: The Irish revolutionary is elected but does not take her seat.
events.description: On December 28, 1918, Constance Markievicz became the first woman elected to the British House of Commons.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 28

events.title: The US Endangered Species Act is signed
events.summary: Richard Nixon signs a landmark wildlife protection law.
events.description: On December 28, 1973, US President Richard Nixon signed the Endangered Species Act into law.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 28

events.title: The Irish Free State becomes Ireland
events.summary: A new constitution renames the state.
events.description: On December 29, 1937, with the enactment of a new constitution, the Irish Free State became known as Ireland.
events.notificationTitle: A new name for a nation
events.notificationBody: In 1937, a new constitution turned the Irish Free State into Ireland.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 29

events.title: The United States annexes Texas
events.summary: The independent Republic of Texas joins the Union.
events.description: On December 29, 1845, the US Congress approved the annexation of the independent Republic of Texas by the United States.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 29

events.title: William Gladstone is born in Liverpool
events.summary: The future four-time British prime minister is born.
events.description: On December 29, 1809, William Ewart Gladstone was born in Liverpool. He served as prime minister of Great Britain four times between 1868 and 1894.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 29

events.title: The Wounded Knee Massacre
events.summary: US troops kill Lakota people at Wounded Knee Creek in South Dakota.
events.description: On December 29, 1890, US Army troops carried out the Wounded Knee Massacre in South Dakota. It was the last major armed conflict between the United States and the Plains peoples.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 29

events.title: Guinea is declared free of Ebola
events.summary: The WHO declares the end of transmission two years after the outbreak began.
events.description: On December 29, 2015, the World Health Organization declared Guinea free of Ebola, some two years after the deadly disease was reported in the country.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 29

events.title: The Soviet Union is established
events.summary: The USSR is founded with its capital in Moscow.
events.description: On December 30, 1922, the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics was established, with its capital in Moscow.
events.notificationBody: In 1922, the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics was established.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 30

events.title: Jose Rizal is executed in Manila
events.summary: The Philippine national hero is put to death by Spanish authorities.
events.description: On December 30, 1896, Jose Rizal, the writer and reformer regarded as a national hero of the Philippines, was publicly executed by the country's Spanish rulers.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 30

events.title: The Gadsden Purchase is signed
events.summary: The United States buys nearly 30,000 square miles from Mexico.
events.description: On December 30, 1853, the United States acquired nearly 30,000 square miles of northern Mexican territory with the signing of the Gadsden Purchase.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 30

events.title: Robert Falcon Scott sets a farthest-south record
events.summary: His party pushes deeper into Antarctica than anyone before.
events.description: On December 30, 1902, the British explorer Robert Falcon Scott set a new record for reaching the farthest point south, on the Ross Ice Shelf.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 30

events.title: The Treaty of Surji-Arjungaon is signed
events.summary: A Maratha chief cedes territory and power in India to the British.
events.description: On December 30, 1803, the Maratha chief Daulat Rao Sindhia signed the Treaty of Surji-Arjungaon, ceding political power and territory in India to the British.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 30

events.title: The first ball drops in Times Square
events.summary: New York City starts a New Year's Eve tradition.
events.description: On December 31, 1907, the first ball was dropped at Times Square in New York City to celebrate New Year's Eve, beginning a tradition that continues today.
events.notificationBody: In 1907, the first New Year's Eve ball dropped in Times Square.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 31

events.title: The English East India Company is chartered
events.summary: A royal charter launches the company for trade with Asia.
events.description: On December 31, 1600, the East India Company, formed to exploit trade with East and Southeast Asia and India, was incorporated by English royal charter.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 31

events.title: Queen Victoria names Ottawa the capital of Canada
events.summary: The city is chosen as the national capital.
events.description: On December 31, 1857, Queen Victoria named Ottawa the national capital of Canada.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 31

events.title: The United States hands the Panama Canal to Panama
events.summary: Panama takes full control of the canal.
events.description: On December 31, 1999, the United States officially handed over control of the Panama Canal to Panama.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 31

events.title: Taipei 101 opens as the world's tallest building
events.summary: The 508-metre tower opens in Taiwan's capital.
events.description: On December 31, 2004, Taipei 101 opened in Taipei, Taiwan. At 1,667 feet (508 metres), it was then the tallest building in the world.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 31

events.title: Eleven countries adopt the euro
events.summary: Europe's single currency is launched.
events.description: On January 1, 1999, eleven European Union countries adopted the euro as their currency.
events.notificationBody: In 1999, eleven European countries adopted the euro.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 1

events.title: Haiti declares independence from France
events.summary: The Haitian Revolution ends with a new independent nation.
events.description: On January 1, 1804, Haiti declared its independence from France, bringing the Haitian Revolution to an end.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 1

events.title: Lincoln issues the Emancipation Proclamation
events.summary: The order frees enslaved people in the Confederacy.
events.description: On January 1, 1863, US President Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation, which freed enslaved people in the Confederacy.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 1

events.title: The World Trade Organization is established
events.summary: A new global body oversees international trade rules.
events.description: On January 1, 1995, the World Trade Organization was formally established.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 1

events.title: Fulgencio Batista flees Cuba
events.summary: Fidel Castro's rebels topple the dictator's regime.
events.description: On January 1, 1959, the dictator Fulgencio Batista fled Cuba after his regime was toppled by rebel forces led by Fidel Castro.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 1
